scenarios.title: The Debut Shirt
scenarios.text: His debut shirt, still damp, is in his kit bag. Everybody wants it: {MUM}, his first coach, a charity auction, the club museum.

choices.label: {MUM}
choices.text: {MUM} frames it in the living room. She tells every visitor the story, with new details each time.

choices.label: Your first coach
choices.text: His first coach hangs it in the clubhouse of his tiny club. Kids train under it every Saturday.

choices.label: Keep it yourself
choices.text: He puts it in a box under his bed. Some nights he takes it out and looks at it.

scenarios.title: The Ball
scenarios.text: The referee hands him the match ball after the final whistle: his first professional goal. Every teammate has signed it. Someone has drawn a moustache on it.

choices.label: Give it to {DAD}
choices.desc: He drove you to every match.
choices.text: {DAD} holds it like a newborn and doesn't speak for a full minute. Then he says, 'I knew.'

choices.label: Post a photo with it
choices.text: The photo with the ball (and the moustache) is his most-liked post ever.

scenarios.title: Hat-Trick
scenarios.text: Three goals. The match ball is his. His phone has two hundred messages. The fans have already made a chant about it. The captain wants to know if he's buying drinks.
scenarios.prompt: How do you celebrate a hat-trick?

choices.label: Dinner for the whole squad
choices.text: He pays for the squad's dinner and thanks every player for every pass. The dressing room loves him.

choices.label: Quiet night with family
choices.text: He goes home and eats {MUM}'s cooking. The match ball sits on the table between the dishes.

choices.label: A big night out
choices.text: A big night. A few too many photos. A great story.

scenarios.title: Silverware
scenarios.text: The trophy is heavier than it looks. Confetti everywhere. Champagne in his eyes. Somewhere in the stands, his family is screaming.

choices.label: Run to the stands with the trophy
choices.text: He climbs into the stands with the trophy. {MUM} holds it and cries. The photo is on every front page.

choices.label: Celebrate with the kit man and staff
choices.text: He hands the trophy to the kit man and the groundsman first. The staff will never forget it.

scenarios.title: Champions
scenarios.text: League champions. The open-top bus parade is tomorrow. A million people are expected. He hasn't slept. He doesn't want to.

choices.label: Lead the singing on the bus
choices.text: He leads the singing on the top deck for four hours. His voice is gone by the end. The videos live forever.

choices.label: Take it all in quietly
choices.text: He stands at the back of the bus and tries to remember every face. It's the happiest day of his life.

scenarios.title: Down
scenarios.text: Relegated. The players sit on the pitch. Fans are crying in the stands. A small boy in his shirt is holding his father's hand, both of them sobbing.

choices.label: Go to the fans and apologise
choices.text: He walks to the stand and applauds them. Some boo. Most applaud back. The boy waves.

choices.label: Promise to bring the club back up
choices.hint: A promise you'll be held to.
choices.text: 'We'll be back. I'll be here.' The fans will hold him to it.

choices.label: Walk straight to the tunnel
choices.text: He walks straight off. Some fans see it as heartbreak. Some see it as abandonment.

scenarios.title: Promoted
scenarios.text: Promotion. The pitch invasion lasts forty minutes. Someone has taken his boots. Someone else has taken a piece of the goal net. Next season: the big league.

choices.label: Celebrate with the fans on the pitch
choices.desc: In the middle of it all.
choices.text: He's lifted onto the fans' shoulders and carried around the pitch. He loses his shirt, his socks and his voice.

choices.label: Think about next season
choices.text: Even in the celebrations, he's thinking about the level above. The manager notices.

scenarios.title: Eighteen
scenarios.text: He's eighteen. Legally an adult. The squad has organised a surprise. {MUM} has organised a different surprise. The two surprises are on the same evening.

choices.label: Go to {MUM}'s first, then the squad's
choices.text: He eats two cakes and hears two very different speeches. Both make him cry, for different reasons.

choices.label: Bring the squad to {MUM}'s
choices.text: Twenty footballers in {MUM}'s living room. She feeds them all. It's the best party anyone has ever been to.

scenarios.title: Thirty
scenarios.text: Thirty. The squad has bought him a walking stick and a pair of slippers. The young players are calling him 'Grandpa'. He's never felt better, apart from his knees.

choices.label: Laugh and use the walking stick in the warm-up
choices.text: He hobbles out for the warm-up with the stick. The crowd loves it. Then he scores.

choices.label: Reflect on the decade
choices.text: He writes a long letter to his twenty-year-old self. It's funny and sad and wise.

scenarios.title: The Walk
scenarios.text: The long walk to the tunnel after the red card. Twenty thousand people watching. The manager won't look at him. A child in the front row is crying.

choices.label: Apologise to the dressing room immediately
choices.text: He apologises to every teammate at full time. Nobody is angry by the end. Mostly.

choices.label: Blame the referee
choices.text: He blames the referee in the tunnel. The replays don't help him.

choices.label: Write to the child in the front row
choices.text: The club finds the child. He sends a signed shirt and a note: 'Sorry I let you down. Never again.'

scenarios.title: Three Defeats
scenarios.text: Three defeats in a row. Training is silent. The manager has called a players-only meeting and left the room.

ok.text: He speaks honestly about his own mistakes first. Others follow. The meeting becomes the turning point of the season.

bad.text: He speaks, but it comes out as blame. The meeting gets worse.

choices.label: Listen
choices.text: He listens. The captain talks. The room settles.

scenarios.title: The Worst Game
scenarios.text: The worst game of his career. Every touch went wrong. The fans booed when he was subbed. The internet is calling him a disgrace.

choices.label: Watch it back, every minute
choices.text: He watches every minute twice. It's agony. By the end he knows exactly what went wrong.

choices.label: Switch off completely
choices.text: Phone off, family, sleep. One bad game. It doesn't define him.

choices.label: Apologise to the fans online
choices.text: 'Not good enough. I'll be better.' The fans respond warmly. Most of them.

scenarios.title: On a Streak
scenarios.text: Three games, three goals. He has worn the same socks, eaten the same breakfast and driven the same route to every match. The socks are becoming a problem.

choices.label: Keep everything the same
choices.text: Same socks. Same breakfast. Same route. The kit man refuses to touch the socks.

choices.label: Wash the socks
choices.text: He washes the socks. The squad gasps. He scores anyway.

scenarios.title: Four Weeks on the Bench
scenarios.text: Four matches on the bench without getting on. His family has stopped asking. His agent has started calling.

choices.label: Ask the manager what's missing
choices.text: The manager gives him two clear things. He works on both. Three weeks later, he's back in.

choices.label: Tell your agent to find a loan
choices.text: His agent starts making calls. The manager hears about it.

choices.label: Be the best substitute in the world
choices.desc: Cheer, warm up hard, be ready.
choices.text: He's the loudest voice on the bench. When his chance comes, he's ready.

scenarios.title: First Choice
scenarios.text: The manager has told him: he's first choice now. The shirt is his. Every week. The pressure feels different when it's yours to lose.

choices.label: Never relax
choices.desc: Work harder than when you were fighting for it.
choices.text: He trains harder than ever. The shirt stays his.

choices.label: Enjoy it
choices.text: He enjoys every minute. His confidence soars. So does his form.

scenarios.title: Frozen Out
scenarios.text: He's been told to train with the youth team. No explanation. His locker has been moved. His name has disappeared from the matchday programme.

choices.label: Train with the youth team like a professional
choices.text: He trains with the kids and helps them. The youth coaches tell the manager. Slowly, the door opens.

choices.label: Demand a transfer
choices.text: He demands a move. The club is happy to oblige.

choices.label: Go public
choices.text: He goes public. The fans are split. The club is furious.

scenarios.title: The Call-Up
scenarios.text: His name is on the national team list. {DAD} heard it on the radio before {J} did and has been crying in the car outside the market for twenty minutes.

choices.label: Call {DAD} first
choices.text: {DAD} can't speak on the phone. {MUM} takes over. Then {SIB}. Then the whole street.

choices.label: Visit your first club
choices.text: He drives to his first club and tells the kids. They lift him on their shoulders.

scenarios.title: The First Night
scenarios.text: First night in a new city. An empty flat, a suitcase, a takeaway, the noise of a city he doesn't know. Tomorrow, he meets his new teammates.
scenarios.prompt: Your first night at a new club.

choices.label: Walk the city
choices.text: He walks for two hours. A bakery, a park, a mosque, a football pitch with kids. The city feels a little more his.

choices.label: Study your new teammates' names
choices.text: He learns every name and number from the squad list. Tomorrow, he greets everyone by name. They notice.

choices.label: Call home for hours
choices.text: He talks to everyone at home. It helps. It also makes it harder.

scenarios.title: On Loan
scenarios.text: A loan player is always a guest. Some teammates will see him as a threat, some as a short-term guy who doesn't care. He has one season to prove both groups wrong.

choices.label: Commit like you're staying forever
choices.text: He commits completely. By Christmas, the fans are asking the club to buy him.

choices.label: Focus on development
choices.text: He focuses on playing and improving. Efficient, a little lonely.

scenarios.title: Back Again
scenarios.text: Back at his parent club after the loan. Some faces are new. Some are gone. The manager says, 'Show me what you learned.'

choices.label: Show him in the first session
choices.text: He's the best player in the first session. The manager raises an eyebrow. Good sign.

choices.label: Reconnect with old teammates first
choices.text: He spends the first week catching up with everyone. The squad feels like home again.

scenarios.title: No Club
scenarios.text: Contract over. No new club yet. For the first time since he was a child, there's no training tomorrow.
scenarios.prompt: Your first day as a free agent.

choices.label: Train alone at 7am anyway
choices.text: A park, a ball, cones, a stopwatch. He trains like he's still at a club.

choices.label: Rest and reflect
choices.text: He sleeps until ten and has breakfast with his family. It's terrifying and lovely.

scenarios.title: One Hundred Thousand
scenarios.text: One hundred thousand followers. {SIB} screenshots it and sends it to the entire family group. {MUM} asks what a follower is.

choices.label: A thank-you video
choices.text: A short thank-you video filmed in his kitchen. Simple. It does well.

choices.label: Explain followers to {MUM}
choices.text: Forty minutes later, {MUM} understands followers and has opened an account. She follows him and nobody else.

scenarios.title: One Million
scenarios.text: One million people follow him. More than the population of the town he grew up in. He stares at the number for a long time.

choices.label: Do something for the town
choices.desc: One for each person back home.
choices.text: He funds a new pitch for his hometown, one 'for every follower', as the local paper puts it.

choices.label: A live Q&A
choices.text: Two hours of questions. Someone asks about his first boots. He gets emotional.

scenarios.title: Season Over
scenarios.text: The last match is over. The stadium empties. He sits alone in the dressing room for a while, boots off, thinking about the season: the good, the bad, the things he'd do differently.

choices.label: Write down three lessons
choices.text: Three lessons in his notes app. He'll read them on the first day of pre-season.

choices.label: Thank the staff before leaving
choices.text: He thanks every member of staff by name. The cook gives him a hug and a container of food.

choices.label: Just go home
choices.text: Home. Sleep. A summer of rest.

scenarios.title: One Hundred
scenarios.text: His hundredth professional appearance. The club has made a special shirt with '100' on the back. His family is in the stands with a homemade banner.

choices.label: Give the shirt to {MUM}
choices.text: {MUM}'s wall is running out of space. She doesn't care.

choices.label: Auction it for charity
choices.text: The shirt raises a lot of money for a children's hospital.

scenarios.title: Goal of the Season?
scenarios.text: His solo goal from last month has been nominated for the league's goal of the season. Fans are voting. A rival's tap-in is somehow leading.

out.text: He wins. The trophy is tiny. He loves it.
The tap-in wins. The internet is outraged on his behalf.

choices.label: Stay quiet
choices.text: He stays out of it and comes second. Fine.

scenarios.title: The Provider
scenarios.text: A stats account points out that he's created more chances than any other player in the league this season. The strikers have started buying him dinner.

choices.label: Credit the strikers
choices.text: 'They do the hard part.' The strikers love him even more.

choices.label: Accept the dinners
choices.text: A season of free dinners. Excellent.

scenarios.title: Clean Sheets
scenarios.text: Five clean sheets in a row. The defence is being called 'the wall'. The goalkeeper has started bringing cake for the defenders after every shut-out.

choices.label: Celebrate as a unit
choices.text: A defenders-only dinner. They plan the next clean sheet like a military operation.

choices.label: Stay humble
choices.text: He credits the strikers' pressing. The whole squad appreciates it.

scenarios.title: Player of the Month
scenarios.text: He's been named the league's player of the month. The trophy is presented before a home match. His face is on a giant banner outside the stadium.

choices.label: Dedicate it to the team
choices.text: He lifts it and points at his teammates. The dressing room loves it.

choices.label: Dedicate it to your family
choices.text: He dedicates it to {MUM} and {DAD}. They watch at home and cry.

scenarios.title: The Armband
scenarios.text: His first match as captain. The armband feels heavier than it looks. Before kick-off, he has to lead the team talk.
scenarios.prompt: Your first team talk as captain.

choices.label: Short and fierce
choices.text: Three sentences. The roar afterwards shakes the dressing room.

ok.text: He talks about the first time he walked into this stadium. Grown men are blinking hard.

bad.text: He loses his words halfway through. The vice-captain finishes for him.

scenarios.title: For the Country
scenarios.text: Representing his country has changed something at home. Strangers stop {DAD} in the street. {MUM}'s friends ask her for tickets. {SIB}'s teachers mention it in class.
scenarios.prompt: Your family is famous by association.

choices.label: Buy tickets for the whole family for the next international
choices.text: The whole family in national colours, singing the anthem. {DAD} cries through it.

choices.label: Visit their neighbourhood in national kit
choices.text: He visits in the national kit. The street throws a party.

scenarios.title: New Season
scenarios.text: Pre-season starts today. New season, new kit, new targets. The coach asks every player to write down one goal for the season and put it in an envelope.
scenarios.prompt: What do you write in the envelope?

choices.label: A football target
choices.text: He writes a number and seals it. Only he and the coach will know.

choices.label: A personal target
choices.desc: Be a better son, partner, friend.
choices.text: He writes something about the people at home. The coach reads it at the end of the season and smiles.
